o1.biggest_strength: It correctly rebuilds onboarding around the two retention signals: typed recurring tasks and signing in on a second device, with good platform branching and calm copy.
o1.biggest_mistake: It uses one of the five onboarding emails for a Pro upsell instead of using every email to build the two habits that drive retention.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the day-14 Pro email with a targeted missing-habit email and keep the whole series focused on recurring tasks plus second-device use.

o2.biggest_strength: It makes the right strategic call: teach only the two habits that predict retention, stop when both are done, and move Pro out of onboarding.
o2.biggest_mistake: There are a few implementation rough edges, especially the contradictory assumption that every button opens the signup platform while the second-device email must send people elsewhere.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the branching rules and polish the conditional fifth email into clean one-button variants that are ready to load into the email tool.

reason: Both are strong, but Output 2 is closer to the retention job I asked for because it drops the upsell and uses the fifth email to push the missing habit. Output 1 has better finished copy in places, but keeping Pro inside the five-email onboarding series is the bigger strategic miss.
